holidays.name: National Open an Umbrella Indoors Day
holidays.description: This is a day for tempting fate. You pop open an umbrella under a roof and see whether the universe punishes you. It's the one day when superstition gets a fair trial, and the umbrella gets to feel dramatic.
holidays.origin: It's an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It seems to have been created to poke fun at the old superstition that an open umbrella indoors brings bad luck. The day lands on the 13th, which suits a holiday about defying bad omens.
holidays.funFact: One popular explanation for the superstition is that rigid, spring-loaded umbrellas in cramped Victorian-era homes could poke people or knock over belongings. The 'bad luck' may have started as a polite way to stop that.

holidays.name: National Earmuff Day
holidays.description: This day celebrates the cozy gadget that saves frozen ears everywhere. Wear your fluffiest pair, and take a moment to thank the teenager who made winter a lot more bearable.
holidays.origin: The day marks the anniversary of the earmuff patent. Chester Greenwood of Farmington, Maine, received it on March 13, 1877. He reportedly invented them at age 15 after his ears got cold while ice skating.
holidays.funFact: Chester Greenwood was honored so thoroughly in Farmington that Maine celebrates Chester Greenwood Day each December, with a parade and plenty of earmuffs.

holidays.name: National K9 Veterans Day
holidays.description: This day honors the military and police working dogs who sniff out danger, stand guard and serve alongside their human partners. Celebrate with extra belly rubs, a treat for your own good dog, or a thank-you to a K9 handler.
holidays.origin: The date marks the 1942 founding of the U.S. Army K-9 Corps, the program that formally trained dogs for military service during World War II.
holidays.funFact: The Army K-9 Corps began in 1942 as 'Dogs for Defense,' a program that took in pets donated by civilian families.
